scope.domain: Distinct primes p<q, including p=2; integer a>=2; N=p^a q; integer 0<=d<q; primitive Nth root zeta; arbitrary binary N-by-N mask R; D[r,c]=R[r,c] zeta^(rc).
scope.theorem: Either D*D=dI or DD*=dI holds for some mask exactly when d=0 or d=p^j with 0<=j<=a and p^j<q.
scope.boundary: d=q has an inherited divisor witness only. The erasure lemma requires strict d<q. No degree above q is classified.
scope.weighted_interface: The accepted weighted prime-power class permits every nonempty square dimension, repeated row and column labels, row amplitudes p^(k_i/2), and both Grams. It gives d=p^b, b<=K+a, K=max k_i. Erasure retains dimension p^a q and has K=0.
scope.original_problem: For the normalized complex Fourier target, spectral norm, invertible M, and at most s=N-d nonzeros in every inverse row, 0<d<q gives Delta(N,N-d)=sqrt(d/N) iff d is an allowed p-power; every other integer d in that sector has a strict infimum gap.
scope.credit: Short-overlap prime-character erasure and its composition with the accepted enlarged prime-power theorem. Prime-power descent, a=1 low-degree semiprime scope, divisor witnesses, and inverse-row criterion and compactness are inherited.
limits: No Fourier or FFT complexity improvement

scope.historical_scope_qualification: The weighted candidate blanket unresolved-work wording is qualified by its independent review. Existing exact values and quantitative bounds remain accepted; only remaining optima and sharper or optimal rates stay open.
scope.packaging: No scientific program executed, no frozen input edited, no external state changed. Source hashes retain their original meaning; turnkey replay is not certified.
